html:
The Statutes of 1600 are the legal basis of San Marino's government, often called the oldest written constitution still in force in the world.

Written in Latin in six books, they gathered earlier laws of the republic and set out the roles of the Grand and General Council and the Captains Regent. They have been changed and added to many times, notably by a declaration of citizens' rights in 1974, but never replaced.

The statutes helped San Marino keep its identity as a republic while the Papal States and later the Kingdom of Italy grew around it. Compare the much younger Norwegian and American constitutions.
sum: The Statutes of 1600 are the legal basis of San Marino's government, often called the oldest written constitution still in force in the world.
